title: In re William Gardner, Case No. 25-157C (Former Deputy Admin/Chief Admin Officer, Dept of Business & Industry)
text:
STATE OF NEVADA
BEFORE THE NEVADA COMMISSION ON ETHICS
In re William Gardner, Ethics Complaint
Former Deputy Administrator/Chief Case No. 25-157C
Administrative Officer,
Department of Business and Industry,
Division of Industrial Relations,
State of Nevada,
Subject./
STIPULATED AGREEMENT
1. PURPOSE: This Stipulated Agreement resolves Ethics Complaint Case
No. 25-157C before the Nevada Commission on Ethics (“Commission”) concerning
William Gardner (“Gardner”), Former Deputy Administrator/Chief Administrative Officer
for the Division of Industrial Relations (“Division”).
2. JURISDICTION: At all material times, Gardner served as the Deputy
Administrator/Chief Administrative Officer for the Division of Industrial Relations and was
a public officer as defined in NRS 281A.160 and NRS 281A.180. The Ethics in
Government Law (“Ethics Law”) set forth in NRS Chapter 281A gives the Commission
jurisdiction over elected and appointed public officers and public employees whose
conduct is alleged to have violated the provisions of NRS Chapter 281A. See NRS
281A.280. The Commission has jurisdiction over Gardner in this matter.
3. PROCEDURAL HISTORY BEFORE COMMISSION:
a. On August 26, 2025, the Commission received Ethics Complaint No. 25-
157C from a member of the public ("Requester") alleging violation of NRS 281A.550.
b. On October 13, 2025, the Commission issued its Order on Jurisdiction and
Investigation regarding the Complaint’s alleged violation of NRS 281A.550.
c. Also on October 13, 2025, the Executive Director sent Gardner a Notice of
Complaint and Investigation with an opportunity for Gardner to submit a response to the
allegations.
Stipulated Agreement
Case No. 25-157C

d. Gardner waived the time requirements for an investigation and review panel
determination pursuant to NRS 281A.725.
e. On November 17, 2025, through his counsel, Gardner provided a timely
response to the allegation.
f. A Review Panel Determination issued on January 21, 2026, found the facts
established credible evidence to support a determination that just and sufficient cause
exists for the Commission to render an opinion in the matter regarding the alleged
violation of NRS 281A.550.
g. In lieu of an adjudicatory hearing before the Commission, the parties
reached an agreement to resolve this matter on the terms reflected in this Stipulated
Agreement (“Agreement”) and now enter into this Agreement.
4. STIPULATED FACTS:
a. Gardner served as the Chief Administrative Officer/Deputy Administrator for
the Nevada Occupational Safety and Health Administration (“OSHA”), Nevada
Department of Business and Industry, Division of Industrial Relations (“Division”) from
July 2021 to August 26, 2025, although Gardner’s last physical day of work was July 28,
2025.
b. Gardner was responsible for overseeing Nevada OSHA, which is tasked
with enforcing workplace safety regulations at businesses in the public and private sector
throughout Nevada pursuant to NRS Chapter 618 and NAC 618.
c. In his position with Nevada OSHA, Gardner was responsible for formulation
of policy contained in NAC 618. Gardner also controlled and influenced OSHA
investigations which affected businesses regulated by NRS 618 and NAC 618.
d. After leaving the OSHA office on July 28, 2025, Gardner began searching
for new employment to continue to provide for his family.
e. Gardner is now employed as a Senior Safety Manager with The PENTA
Building Group (“PENTA”) responsible for quality assurance programs and workplace
safety. Gardner has no contact with PENTA regarding possible employment prior to July
28, 2025.
Stipulated Agreement
Case No. 25-157C
Page 2 of 6

f. On August 21, 2025, Gardner submitted an email to an OSHA employee
with an application to serve as a Safety Coordinator for an Owner Consolidated Insurance
Program (“OCIP”). This program is governed under NRS 616B.725(3).
5. TERMS / CONCLUSIONS OF LAW: Based on the foregoing, Gardner and the
Commission agree as follows:
a. Each of the stipulated facts enumerated in Section 4 of this Agreement is
agreed to by the parties.
b. Gardner was a public officer as defined in NRS 281A.160 and NRS
281A.180.
c. Gardner’s course of conduct resulted in a single non-willful violation of NRS
281A.550. 1
d. Based upon the consideration and application of the statutory factors set
forth in NRS 281A.775, Gardner and the Commission agree that pursuant to NRS
281A.170 one non-willful violation will be imposed under NRS 281A.550 based on the
following considerations:
1) Public Policy: Violations of the cooling off provisions found in NRS 281A.550
are serious and can undermine the public’s faith in government. However,
in this instance Gardner had no pre-departure discussions with PENTA and
the investigation revealed no facts regarding Gardner taking action while at
OSHA to favor PENTA in exchange for future employment.
2) Previous History: Gardner has not previously been the subject of any
violation of the Ethics Law.
3) Cost of Investigation and Proceedings: Gardner was diligent to cooperate
with and participate in the Commission’s investigation and resolution of this
matter. Because Gardner was willing to resolve the matter prior to an
adjudicatory hearing, significant Commission resources were preserved.
4) Prompt correction of the violation: Gardner did submit a request for an
Advisory Opinion prior to the Complaint being filed in this matter but after
accepting employment at PENTA. Although the timing of Gardner’s request
1 Willful violation means a violation where the public officer acts intentionally and knowingly. NRS
281.A.170
Stipulated Agreement

would have precluded him from the relief available pursuant to NRS
281A.550, several factors established in the statute weigh in Gardner’s
favor including the broad jurisdiction of OSHA, the importance of workplace
safety for Nevadans, and no other indicators of ethical issues surrounding
the circumstances.
5) Financial Gain: Gardner received financial gain from the new employment
but there is no evidence of any special bonuses or gain beyond a standard
employment salary.
6) Additional Factors: In its review of the investigation in total the Review Panel
made special note of the broad jurisdiction of OSHA and requested the
Commission consider that information and the circumstances of Gardner’s
separation from State service when determining an appropriate remedy.
e. Gardner agrees to not consult or lobby on any Nevada OHSA related items
for PENTA, regardless of whether or not they were issues before the agency while he
was there, prior to August 26, 2026 and to otherwise comply with the requirements of
NRS 281A.410.
f. Gardner agrees to successfully complete Cooling Off training as approved
by the Executive Director within 60 days of approval of this agreement. He also agrees to
provide the PENTA human resources team with information related to the Ethics Law’s
Cooling Off requirements.
g. This Agreement is based on the specific facts, circumstances, and law now
before the Commission. Facts or circumstances that differ from those present in this
matter may create a different resolution.
h. This Agreement is not intended to be applicable to or create any admission
of liability by Gardner for any other proceeding against or involving Gardner, and such
use is prohibited to the extent permitted by the jurisdiction of the Commission. If the
Commission rejects this Agreement, none of the provisions herein shall be considered by
the Commission or be admissible as evidence in a hearing on the merits in this matter.
Stipulated Agreement
Case No. 25-157C

6th March

6. WAIVER
a. Gardner knowingly and voluntarily waives his right to a hearing before the
full Commission on the allegations in Ethics Complaint Case No. 25-157C and all rights
he may be accorded with in regard to this matter pursuant to NRS Chapter 281A, the
regulations of the Commission (NAC Chapter 281A), the Nevada Administrative
Procedures Act (NRS Chapter 233B), and any other applicable provisions of law.
b. Gardner knowingly and voluntarily waives his right to any judicial review of
this matter as provided in NRS Chapter 281A, NRS Chapter 233B, or any other applicable
provisions of law.
7. ACCEPTANCE: We, the undersigned parties, have read this Agreement,
understand each and every provision therein, and agree to be bound thereby once
approved by the Commission. In addition, the parties orally agreed to be bound by the
terms of this Agreement during the regular meeting of the Commission on March 18,
2026.2
